name: Daria Santos

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government. This is confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and a junior agent on calls and chats at the contact centre. I finished secondary school, earn near the low end, and still ask for help on complicated returns. I use AI tools every day to draft a reply or find a policy, then check the result because I have sent one wrong answer before.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Tomas, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. Tomas has shifts at a warehouse, and we have less than a month of expenses saved. There are few other centres nearby. I enjoy finding a faster way through a queue, but my own call times are still above target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI Plateau looks like the draft tool I already use, with a person checking the answer. I would share the shortcut I found for finding a return policy, but not send the draft blind.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the job stays, which is a relief, but the money is still tight. Tomas can have a short warehouse week, and our savings would not cover one mortgage payment plus food.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls, check my drafts and show another junior agent the return-policy search. In the first year of small change, I’d move one small weekly purchase into a mortgage reserve instead of buying another phone app.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the house, even with work stable. I can improve my call time and still miss the mortgage if my partner Tomas loses warehouse hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What small purchase could move to savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would drop the extra drink I buy at the bus stop after late shifts. That is not a big sum, but I can put it into an account that is only for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What error made you check drafts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The tool once pulled the wrong return window for an opened item. I caught it after a customer asked again, and since then I open the policy page before giving a date.

say: I’d share the **return-policy shortcut** with other agents on my team.
I’d tell them to **check every draft** against the actual policy before sending.
think: I think the **job remains**, which helps.
I fear Tomas’s **short warehouse week** could still break our budget.
do: Keep **taking calls** and checking drafts in 2026.
Put **bus-stop drink money** into a mortgage reserve during the first year.
feel: **Anxious** about the house despite stable work.
S0.quote: I can improve my call time and still miss the mortgage if my partner Tomas loses warehouse hours.
fieldNote: Her **mortgage anxiety** comes from current household income swings.
She uses **AI daily** but checks an opened-item return rule after an error.
She chooses a **small repeat expense** to start saving.

steps.text: Keep taking calls and verifying draft replies against return policy pages
Save the cost of a weekly bus-stop drink toward the mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take routine replies quickly, because the tool already drafts them for me. I would ask to test the harder refund queue before anyone calls us ready for new work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my easy chats could disappear and leave me with only cases I am still slow at. Tomas’s warehouse hours can dip, so our mortgage is exposed if my roster falls too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for a paid trial on the refund queue and use the new answer tool on sample cases, checking each against the real policy. In the first year routine chats move, I’d apply for a posted service-desk role with enough hours for our mortgage and stop paying for the children’s streaming subscription if my hours fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, with some energy to try. I like learning a system, but I need paid hours. A new skill does not pay a mortgage until someone gives me hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the trial need?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my supervisor to put one paid trial shift on the rota and tell me which mistakes count. If there is no paid slot, I would practise on the current calls but not give up a wage to volunteer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you cut at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Tomas (my partner) that we can cut streaming first, not school meals. We would use the saved amount for the mortgage until my hours settle.

say: I’d ask for a **paid refund trial** before changing my work.
I’d say **routine replies** could move quickly to software.
think: I think my **easy chats** may vanish while I am slow on disputes.
I fear the **mortgage** if both our rosters fall.
do: Take a **paid refund trial** if offered, checking new-tool answers in 2026.
Seek **posted desk work** and cut streaming if hours fall in the first year.
feel: **Alarmed**, but willing to test a real shift.
S1.quote: A new skill does not pay a mortgage until someone gives me hours.
fieldNote: She demands **paid time** for a trial while protecting current wages.
Her **daily AI use** does not shield her junior call tasks.
She would cut **streaming** before school meals.

steps.text: Take a paid refund-queue trial using the new answer tool if offered
Apply for a posted service-desk role with mortgage-covering hours if calls fall
Cancel children’s streaming subscription if her roster shrinks

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the shift AGI by 2028 could do the replies, policy search and hard thinking too. I would ask for posted human roles with wages and dates before the rota changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think AGI could take most of my shift in 2028, even though I use AI every day. Robots around 2031 are later and do not protect a headset worker; less than a month saved would not keep our mortgage current for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for a written staffing date, build a list of openings at the few centres nearby and pause replacing our old car. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid front-desk job whose hours cover mortgage and food, and ask Tomas’s family for a short bridge only if there is a pay gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, almost panicked when I picture the bank letter, but I have a first list to make. I cannot turn a new screen into next month's mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say about the car?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Tomas (my partner) to keep the old car running if it is safe, even if it looks tired. A replacement loan would take the little room we still have.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could family cover a gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomas’s mother could perhaps cover one grocery week, but I would ask only after we know the shift is gone. I cannot count her help as a plan because she has her own bills.

say: I’d ask for **posted paid roles** before the 2028 rota changes.
I’d say **thinking AI** reaches calls before robots.
think: I think AGI could take **most of my shift** despite my daily tool use.
I know **thin savings** will not carry the mortgage for long.
do: Get **staffing dates**, watch vacancies and defer a car loan only while the old car is safe.
Seek **mortgage-covering front-desk work** after 2028; ask whether family can bridge a pay gap.
feel: **Alarmed**, nearly panicked by a possible missed mortgage.
S2.quote: I cannot turn a new screen into next month's mortgage payment.
fieldNote: She understands **2028 thinking AI** threatens a headset job first.
She delays a **car loan** to preserve mortgage room.
Family help is **conditional** and cannot be counted as regular income.

steps.text: Keep the old car instead of replacing it only while safe to drive
Apply for a posted front-desk job covering mortgage and food after 2028
Ask whether Tomas’s mother can spare one grocery week if pay stops

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us time to test where people still need help. I would ask for paid practice on cases the tool cannot settle, with a posted job at the end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think five years could let me get better at difficult returns and move into a service desk, but I do not know how many such jobs survive AGI. Our mortgage still needs cash each month while I learn.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d ask for one paid difficult-case shift a month and practise the account checks with a senior agent if the centre agrees. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for a posted service-desk role with mortgage-covering hours; I would take a short course only if that employer funds it for the posted job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I can make a real trial fit around the children’s school days. Five years before AGI in 2031 gives me time to see whether service-desk work pays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the senior agent to show me three returns that were rejected for different reasons. I would write down what I checked and compare it with the real policy, not just the AI draft.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you study at night?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Tomas (my partner) the course is worth an evening only with a funded place and a vacancy. We cannot pay fees for a promise while the mortgage waits.

say: I’d demand a **posted job** at the end of a training path.
think: I think I could improve at **difficult returns** in five years.
I still need **monthly mortgage cash** while learning.
do: Take **paid difficult-case shifts** if offered from 2026.
Apply for **posted service-desk work** after 2031; take only employer-funded required training.
feel: **Anxious**, but able to test work around school days.
S3.quote: Five years before AGI in 2031 gives me time to see whether service-desk work pays.
fieldNote: She asks for **paid real cases** rather than unpaid study.
Her course condition includes **employer funding** and a posted vacancy.
The **children’s school** affects when she can practise.

steps.text: Take one paid difficult-case shift monthly with a senior agent if offered
Apply for a posted service-desk role with mortgage-covering hours after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to learn difficult cases and save, but I would still ask for paid time to practise. New tools are easier to trust when I can check them on a real account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can get better at the job by 53 and perhaps build a bigger reserve. Full AGI might still take phone thinking work in 2036, and robots around 2039 do not make my headset safer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the call job, put a small amount into savings each pay and take paid practice on the difficult queue if offered. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for a posted customer desk job with hours covering our mortgage and keep the children in their school unless a signed offer made a move safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the mortgage, but not frozen by a date ten years away. I have until AGI arrives in 2036 to learn in pieces, while needing a pay packet next Friday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you practise each week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would practise one hard return each week with a senior agent on paid time if the rota allows it. I would keep my AI draft beside the policy page and check which line it missed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would move only if Tomas (my partner) and I saw a written wage that pays the mortgage and a safe school route for the children. A job title alone will not move our family.

say: I’d ask for **paid practice** on difficult cases.
I’d say ten years lets me **check new tools** against real accounts.
think: I think I can **improve** by 53 and save more.
I know **2036 AGI** may still take my phone work.
do: Keep **calling**, save each pay and practise on paid time if offered.
Apply for **posted desk work** after 2036 only with mortgage-covering hours.
feel: **Anxious** about current bills, but not frozen by 2036.
S4.quote: I have until AGI arrives in 2036 to learn in pieces, while needing a pay packet next Friday.
fieldNote: She continues **daily tool use** but wants more difficult-case skill.
Her **mortgage and school route** constrain any move.
A long horizon does not erase **current bills**.

steps.text: Keep taking call and chat shifts while they pay the mortgage
Save a small amount from each pay toward household costs
Practise one hard return weekly on paid time if the rota allows
Apply for a posted desk role after 2036 with mortgage-covering hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 scares me most. Even the policy search and reply work I do every day could be cheaper with AGI, and our mortgage cannot wait for a long search. I would need a paid trial for a posted role with enough hours to cover our bills and early notice if my shift is cut.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: I wish you had asked what the children see. I try a new tool because I want to keep my children’s home, not because every new screen is exciting.

headlineQuote: I try a new tool because I want to keep my children’s home, not because every new screen is exciting.
portrait: At **43**, Daria is a junior call agent still learning difficult cases after secondary school.
She and Tomas have **two children**, a mortgage, low pay and less than one month saved.
She uses **AI daily** and quickly tests tools, while checking replies after an earlier mistake.
She seeks **paid trials** and real vacancies because few nearby centres offer a fallback.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could take her routine screen tasks before her household builds a reserve.
whatWouldHelp: A **paid trial**, posted job with bill-covering hours and early notice would help.
